prompt.en: Grassroots institutions take Indian democracy beyond elections. Explain how, with reference to active Gram Sabhas and women's reservation in local bodies.

label.en: Explains that active Gram Sabhas give villagers a direct part in decision-making between elections

level1.en: After an election is over, where in a village can ordinary citizens still take part in decisions?

clue.en: In an active Gram Sabha the villagers themselves meet with a proper quorum, keep records, and act on education, sanitation and welfare, so their part does not end after voting.

level2Template.en: An active Gram Sabha keeps villagers directly involved in ___ between elections.

label.en: States that reservation gives women a set share of the seats in local bodies, so that they take part in decisions

rubric.level1: What do the Constitution's rules provide for women in local bodies?

clue.en: Not less than one-third of the seats filled by direct election are reserved for women, and many States have raised this to 50%, so women take part in making the decisions.

level2Template.en: Articles 243(d) and 243(t) reserve not less than ___ of the seats filled by direct election in local bodies for women.

label.en: Concludes that such participation makes democracy more responsive, inclusive and effective at all levels

level1.en: What happens to decisions when the people affected by them help to make them?

clue.en: Jethipura's Gram Sabhas and South Manubankul's women-friendly panchayat show that when citizens take part at the grassroots, democracy becomes more responsive, inclusive and effective.

level2Template.en: Wide participation at the grassroots makes Indian democracy more responsive and ___ at all levels.

text.en: Democracy goes further when citizens take part beyond voting, in the institutions closest to them.
An active Gram Sabha keeps villagers directly involved in decision-making between elections: it meets with a quorum, keeps records, and acts on education, sanitation and welfare.
Articles 243(d) and 243(t) reserve not less than one-third of the seats filled by direct election in local bodies for women, so women take part in making decisions.
Together these make Indian democracy more responsive, inclusive and effective at all levels, as villages like Jethipura and South Manubankul show.
